summary: Adversarial pre-landing review of the supervisor (rollout step 2): 6 lens finders, per-lens refuters, one synthesis
logs: 31 findings from 6 lenses go to synthesis

must_fix.title: False urgent R6 and then R6b at the session open whenever a news position is held overnight
must_fix.where: ai-trader/aitrader/supervise.py:1054-1077. look() judges stale stops on _stamp_ages whenever the beat says market_open. _looks and _stamp_ages at :357-368 fall back to stops_checked_at and measure the age in wall-clock time. The mark's stop at :1034-1035 has the same problem. On the engine side: news_live.py:1575-1619. step() skips the early look when a step began before 09:30, then writes the 'poll', 'quotes' and 'score' beats with market_open taken at write time and checked_at still null until the end look. The per-quote beat at :982 is written before :1017 stamps _covered. adopt_previous at :1645-1652 carries yesterday's stops_checked_at.
must_fix.scenario: BBB is held overnight, which max_hold_days 5 makes normal. The 08:07 child carries over yesterday's last look, about 16:00. The first beats with market_open true are written before this process has looked at the stop: the poll, quotes and score beats of a step that crosses 09:30 (the score call can take up to 90 s), or each per-quote beat when 2+ names are held. Those beats carry an age of about 63,000 s, or about 236,000 s on a Monday. That is above stops_stale_seconds 120. The parent writes stale_stops start and sends an urgent R6: 'מנוע החדשות חי, אבל הסטופים לא נבדקו כבר 63001 שניות (BBB). כנראה המחירים מ-Yahoo מגיעים לאט'. R6b follows once the look lands. The 09:30 mark also books stale_stops seconds that feed R11. Both verifiers reproduced it on the real NewsTrader and through supervise.main. They disagreed only on how often it happens. One verifier said about 7% of mornings with one name; the other said one name is enough on any step that crosses 09:30. My own reading of step() supports the wider window (the scorer phase lies inside it). In both readings it is near-certain with 2+ names. Ruling 45 fixed the same overnight stamp for handover_s only. Ruling 35 covers restarts inside the session, not the closed night. This is a recurring false urgent line about stops, and its stated cause is false.
must_fix.fix: In look(), count stamp ages in market-open seconds only. The smallest form caps each age and the unknown-stamp `born` at the seconds since today's session open, next to Ruling 53's resume cap. The cleaner form uses open_seconds(stamp, now, cal), the measure blind_s and gap_line already use. Apply the same cap to R6's {s}, to the stale_stops row's stop and to the mark's stop, so neither the line nor R11 counts the night. Add one test: yesterday's stamp and a beat with market_open true at 09:30:05 give no stale_stops row and no R6; at 09:32:05, with the stamp still old, R6 goes out with s about 125. A late first start (12:40) still gets an R6 at its boot beat with this fix. That is Ruling 35's accepted case, and must-fix 2's R4 goes beside it.

must_fix.title: No R4 when the day's first parent comes up late after a normal close (a regression: tonight's slot prompt drops the old 'engine was down' push)
must_fix.where: ai-trader/aitrader/supervise.py:454-457. gap_line returns None after a sup_stop whose why has no R4b word; the docstring at :441-443 names end_of_day and closed_today. It is called from up() at :1160-1164, with prev = the last row (:851). The old prompt, news-watch.md at 95d51f44 line 6, pushed 'the engine was down' itself when it started the engine after 09:30. Task 19's news-watch.md (commit 9663262 on supervisor-build, which lands with this wave) no longer does; R4 was meant to own that line.
must_fix.scenario: Thursday ends normally with sup_stop end_of_day at 16:05:01. On Friday the 08:07, 08:37 and 09:07 slots fail on the shared usage limit, which happened on 2026-11-11 and 11-12 (progress.md:239). The 09:37 slot (or the 12:37 one) launches, and the first up comes at 09:40 (or 12:40). gap_line returns None, although open_seconds is 600 (or 11,400); the verifier ran it. With nothing held, the owner gets no line until R11 at 16:22 NY, and only if the close slot runs. With names held, the only line is the boot-beat R6, which blames a slow Yahoo. The brief's reason for the None ('R5a-R5e said that the stops are not checked') does not hold for end_of_day or closed_today, because no line said anything. A line that should go out never does.
must_fix.fix: In gap_line, treat a prev sup_stop whose why is 'end_of_day' or 'closed_today' like a row that is no sup_stop, so R4 applies. open_seconds already gives 0 on a normal night and on closed days, so this adds no noise. Update the docstring. Add tests: prev = Thursday's 16:05:01 end_of_day and an up on Friday at 12:40 gives R4 with s 11400; the same prev and an up on Friday at 08:05 gives None. Optional, and the same change as should-fix time-4: when prev is from an earlier NY day, show max(prev.t, today's open) as {time}, so the line does not read 'from 23:05' (yesterday).

must_fix.title: Drill a prints PASS when an episode says R1 twice: it cannot see 'one R1 per episode'
must_fix.where: ai-trader/scripts/drill_supervisor.py:178-180: said() counts only alert ids with sent true. :343-349: the waits before each kill and after the last only ask for >= k. :381 is the final check. The hourly cap at supervise.py:410-433, with config.json max_alerts_per_hour 6, equals KILLS = 6.
must_fix.scenario: The verifier made a private mutant whose second episode says R1 twice. `drill_supervisor.py a --fast` still printed `PASS a kills=6+1 ... r1=6+1`. The rows were R1-1, R1-2 and R1-3 (both for kill 2), then R1-4 to R1-6. After kill 6 the wait for >= 6 was already met, so the parent was stopped before kill 6's own R1. Had that R1 been said, it would have been the 7th counted line of the hour: held back as capped and not counted by said(). Drill a is the only check of many episodes under one parent; the unit test covers one episode. Spec 11.2 lists 'one R1 per episode' as a pass mark of step 2. This is a drill that can print PASS while the property it gates is broken.
must_fix.fix: Count R1 alert ids whatever `sent` says (capped rows keep kind R1). After each wait before kill k, fail unless there are exactly k ids. After the last wait, settle for a few ticks and require exactly KILLS ids, all with sent true; require exactly 1 in the engine part. Keep Ruling P3: same six kills and same cap, and max_alerts_per_hour is not raised. Re-run the duplicate-R1 mutant and see FAIL before the landing run.

should_fix.title: R11 goes out on every clean trading day, and the handover bookkeeping overstates the minutes without stop checks
should_fix.where: ai-trader/aitrader/uptime.py:46-50 (every exit-to-up after a handover is booked as unprotected), :60-66 (a pair whose later mark has a null hb is booked as gap for the whole pair), :222-225 and :238 (R11 counts as told only R4/R4b rows); supervise.py:987-990 (watch returns 'handover' before look, so the handover minute gets no mark) and :248-250 (the new parent's first mark has a null hb)
should_fix.fix: (a) Write the minute's mark before watch returns 'handover', or book a null-hb pair as gap only from the last exit or sup_stop row inside it. Golden test: one 46 s handover gives unprotected_s 46, not 107. (b) Count handover stretches under outage_report_seconds as reported, or fire R11 only when the untold seconds reach outage_report_seconds. Test: four handovers under 60 s and no fall send no R11. Until (b) lands, or the controller amends spec 11.2's first-day item 'a quiet phone', that check fails by construction on day 1. Decide before the first live day. The bias in (a) alone also puts a perfect day under the 99% uptime that decides question 3 (move to a paid server). Severity: finder and verifier agree on should-fix. Under the literal must-fix wording, a wrong number about stops is borderline, but it errs toward caution.

should_fix.title: R4c names the positions of the day's last up, not the book
should_fix.fix: Take R4c's {held} from news_book.json read as plain JSON, as supervise._held_now already does. Fall back to the last up's held only when the book cannot be read. This goes against Ruling P11, with harm shown. When a position changed after the last up and an outage is open at the close, R4c names a name that was sold and omits a name that is held unprotected, and it contradicts the R3/R3b of the same day.

should_fix.title: Relayed unsent lines carry no time, so present-tense alarms reach the owner after the engine has recovered
should_fix.where: ai-trader/aitrader/supervise.py:638-641 (unsent entries are {id, kind, text}); finish() at :949-959 gives the lines in flight only 5 s; the relay is news-watch.md step 3
should_fix.fix: Add the first row's `t` to each unsent entry, and have the relay prefix it ('נשלח באיחור, מ-HH:MM שעון ישראל'). Leave out an R6 whose R6b went out with sent true. This touches the slot prompt as well as supervise.py.

should_fix.title: One outage is told twice across days (R4c at the close, then R4 or R4b the next morning), and earlier-day seconds count as today's reported seconds in R11
should_fix.where: ai-trader/aitrader/supervise.py:449-457 (gap_line counts session seconds of earlier days); uptime.py:221-235 (R4c is suppressed only by today's told rows)
should_fix.fix: When prev is from an earlier NY day, count s from today's open and show today's open as {time}. Or skip R4/R4b when that day's R4c was sent. This is naturally done in the same edit as must-fix 2.

should_fix.title: No 'back' line after an urgent R3, R3c or R5c when the relaunch comes back quickly
should_fix.where: ai-trader/aitrader/supervise.py:450-457 (no line under outage_report_seconds); ownerlines.py:92 (WORDS['R4b.why'] has no lock_held)
should_fix.fix: At the first up after a sup_stop of crash_loop or lock_held, send a short line whatever the gap: R4b without the threshold for these causes, or a new id in ownerlines with a word for lock_held. This follows the spec's letter, so it is a design gap and not a coding slip.

should_fix.title: Drill e's PASS does not depend on check 4: no mismatch is ever produced
should_fix.fix: Plant one deterministic mismatch per run: after a kill, append a BUY row of a name the book does not hold, then require the book_mismatch row and E1. Or print `mismatch_clause=not_exercised` so the PASS is not read as coverage. Check 4 and E1 are pinned by unit tests, so nothing broken lands through this gap alone.

should_fix.title: Dead-man (Task 21/22): a confirmed cancel leaves news_deadman.json armed, so every morning books a phantom new_seq alarm
should_fix.fix: In Task 21, after a confirmed cancel (at the close, or a trip or halt with said), clear due_at. Or put the old due_at on the new_seq row and count only messages that were neither cancelled nor replaced. Must land before deadman.enabled is turned on and before the two-week report decides question 3. Inert tonight.

minor: lifecycle-1: with the hang switch on, R2 is said only at the replacement's first up (supervise.py:1156-1159). A planned end (handover, signal, orphaned) between the hang kill and that up drops R2 with no alert row, so --status cannot relay it. The verifier reproduced it and corrected the window to seconds (boot plus first look), not 300 s. R6 during the hang and R11 partly cover it. It is the same 'silent line' class as must-fix 2, and the fix is cheap: before the planned-end branch at :1227 (and the halt, lock and trip ends), send R2 or write an unsent row. It can ride in the same round.

lifecycle-2: the loop form with --state-dir or --config and no child_cmd still starts the live engine on the live book and watches the wrong heartbeat. With the switch on it kills a healthy engine, and after 5 restarts the owner gets a false R3. This is operator misuse only; no drill, test or launch path does it. Fix: refuse a non-ROOT --state-dir or --config with exit 2 when child_cmd is None, as clear_halt does (supervise.py:805-808).

lifecycle-3 + engine-2 (merged; both about config.json supervisor._note on planned_stop_grace_seconds): the note guards mark_gap_max_seconds, but --status uses parent_stale_seconds. Worst case: last mark about 60 s old, plus grace 120, plus send_timeout 5, is about 185 s against 180. The note also ignores the step's closing sends (the look's own line, the closing resend and the late-line retry, each up to 15 s), which can push a planned stop past 120 s into a group SIGKILL during an ntfy outage. No harm tonight: the verifiers showed only finish() rows are exposed for at most 5 s, the kill is filed as planned, and in an outage nothing was told, so no duplicate. But following the note when guards go to 'enforce' would make replace_parent readable while the engine is still stopping. Fix: rewrite the note as parent_stale_seconds >= planned_stop_grace_seconds + 60 + send_timeout_seconds plus the closing sends, raise the keys together, and optionally skip the step-tail late-line retry when STOP is set.

lifecycle-4: a timely planned stop never signals the child's process group (supervise.py:1184-1191), so trial `claude -p` grandchildren started by _ask_later (news_live.py:1416-1436) outlive the engine, and their 60 s timeout dies with it. They hold no lock and write no state. The verifier reproduced it. One-line fix: call _signal_group(child.pid, SIGKILL) after the planned wait returns (Ruling 36f says this is safe).
ownerlines-6: a stale-stops episode that opened with only blind names (so its R6 was suppressed) never sends R6 for a non-blind name that goes stale later (supervise.py:1065-1077). Rare.

ownerlines-7: R1's {sold} says 'בסטופ' for every SELL since the last exit, including owner exit requests and time exits (supervise.py:1141-1144, ownerlines.py:120-127). List only sales whose reason is a stop under that word. Its TypeError half is unreachable (see refuted robustness-2), but using held_text's stop_text in sold_text is a cheap consistency fix.

ownerlines-8: a halt under the parent gives two urgent lines: the engine's own calendar or chain line (news_live.py:1885-1891, 1916-1921, 1984-1989), then R5b or R5a. The spec keeps this on purpose (spec 3 row 12, spec 8). Gate the engine's line on supervised is None, or record the choice.

ownerlines-9: with no ntfy channel, the engine counts a line as told once it is in the log (news_live.py:1489, 1237, E1). Under the parent that log is .cache/news_live.log, which nobody relays. Latent: the live environment has the topic, and the child inherits it. Fix: have the landing check that the topic variable is set (print set or unset only, never the value).

time-5 (lowered from should-fix to minor; the verifier's evidence is solid): before each hang kill, R6 goes out first, then R6b, then R2, because stops_stale_seconds 120 < hang_seconds 180. The same pair comes at the boot beat after a slow restart. This is by design under Ruling P16 (R6 fires during a long call) and Ruling 35. The real defect is the test: test_supervise.py:1298-1303 runs hang 1 < stale 2, the opposite order to config.json, so its name claims more than it proves. Re-run it with stale < hang.

time-6: an R6 episode still open at the bell is ended by market_open turning false (supervise.py:1055, :1072-1077), and R6b then says the stops are checked again. Fix: end it with only the row and no R6b when the market has closed.

engine-1: a planned stop that cuts a first start's priming still writes the 'primed' row (news_live.py:796-797). _run then throws the marks away (:1960-1962), so the next start writes a second primed row for the same headlines. Measurement only, and news_seen_log.jsonl is tracked. Fix: skip the row when STOP.is_set().

gate-3 (lowered from should-fix to minor; spec 5.1's order is pinned by test_news_supervised.py:900-916, :982-993): drill a's 'first look within 3 s' passes with the start's first look removed, because code_stamp, feed and send are instant stubs (engine_child.py:113-126). Its engine_look_s is stub timing, not evidence of the order. Possible fix: give the stubs slow modes such as commit_delay_s and feed_delay_s.

gate-5: drill g never holds a merge open during a start and never touches state/, so it passes with tree_busy disabled (rc7=0 in every run). It is a smoke test of restarts beside git, not evidence for spec 4.7's guard; the 7 path is unit-tested. Fix: one conflicting merge held open during some starts, requiring rc7 >= 1.

gate-6: drill e's bare engine (--until 24:00, no --supervised) survives a SIGKILL sent to the drill script's pid alone. The tripwire keeps it harmless. Fix: start bare engines with --supervised os.getpid(), and have signal_child also check that the drill's state path is in argv.

gate-7: cloud-check --alive passes on a single mark after sup_start without reading its age or hb (drill_supervisor.py:737-743). The cloud parent's last stdout line (supervise.py:1257, AFTER) names --status with no --state-dir, so it points at the live directory. No harm after the close. Fix: require a fresh mark with a non-null hb, and print the state dir in cloud mode.

gate-8 (Task 21): drain() drops every Sender result whose tag is not a pending owner line (supervise.py:927-947). Sender.close() only queues None on a daemon worker and main does not wait (deadman.py:95-98), so a later leave ping could die with the interpreter. Inert tonight; Ruling P26 already gives tag routing to Task 21.
refuted: robustness-1: refuted. The verifier showed no input the parent really meets reaches the unguarded loop path. Every real read is type-guarded, and the state file is written only by save_state with ints via tmp+rename. The PDEATHSIG SIGKILL on a parent crash is the designed protection against an unwatched engine, and exit code 1 is handled by R12 plus a relaunch. Keep 'wrap look()'s bookkeeping, move finish() into a finally, type-check load_state' as backlog hardening.

robustness-2: refuted. No SELL with a null or missing stop can enter R1's window: _buy sets stop_price in the same block as the fill, before any save, and _sell copies it. The cited 2026-11-10 MU row has no stop but falls before `ref`. Ruling 38 deferred this class, and the verifier re-checked the reason at d639d8ec. The real wording issue survives as ownerlines-7.

lifecycle-1 (partial): the finding's 300 s window is wrong. A no-quote name enters the beat's blind list at its first look (news_live.py:1225), so the loss window is boot plus first look, a few seconds. The finding is kept as minor.

lifecycle-3 (partial): the claimed harm today does not hold. The mark age passes 180 s only after the grace, when the child has already been killed, so only finish()'s rows (at most 5 s) are exposed, and the :07/:37 watchdog reads do not overlap. Kept as a minor note for future tuning.

engine-2 (partial): the 'duplicate late line' and 'lost stopping beat' harms are refuted. In the outage nothing was told, so the next 'דווח באיחור' is the first delivery. Nothing reads the 'stopping' phase. The SIGKILL is the designed bound and is filed as planned. Kept, merged with lifecycle-3.

ownerlines-1 (partial): 'every trading morning' is overstated. With one held name and a step that starts after the bell, the stale beat lives only milliseconds. The severity stands, because steps that cross 09:30 and mornings with 2+ names make it recurrent (see must-fix 1).
synth.verdict:
Yes, tonight's landing can go ahead once the three must-fix items are in: two small changes in ai-trader/aitrader/supervise.py, each with one test (count stop-look age in market-open seconds only; R4 after an end_of_day or closed_today sup_stop), and one change in ai-trader/scripts/drill_supervisor.py (count R1 ids exactly, then re-run the duplicate-R1 mutant to see FAIL). The full suite and drills a-g must then re-run green. Best done in the same pre-landing round as the planned Task 14f. lifecycle-1 is optional in that round: the same silent-line class, one guard. No lens found two engines, an engine nobody watches, a delayed or skipped stop look, a parent crash on input it will really meet, a leak of topic or exception text, or any change to buy, sell or stop behaviour. On severity, I took the verifier's lower rating for time-5 and gate-3; both rest on cited rulings and unit tests, not thin evidence. Note that must-fix 2 is a regression made by Task 19's prompt (commit 9663262), which is not in 95d51f44..d639d8ec but lands with this wave. What to watch in the drills:
- Drill a: exactly 6 R1 ids in the dummy part and 1 in the engine part, none capped.
- Drill b: one hang row and one R2.
- Drill e's mismatches=0 and drill g's rc7=0 are expected, and they are not evidence for check 4 or for the spec 4.7 git rule (unit tests carry those). Drill a's engine_look_s is stub timing.
- Cloud drills: record which signal TaskStop and the 2-hour cap send, and confirm in /proc that no parent or engine survives the stop. cloud-check --alive alone proves only one tick.
On the first live day:
- Expect R11 at 16:22 from handover seconds. Spec 11.2's 'quiet phone' item cannot pass until the R11 should-fix lands or the controller amends the checklist; decide that before day 1.
- At the first open with an overnight-held name, confirm there is no R6 at 09:30.
- At each handover (09:18, 10:48, 12:28, 14:17), read the exit-to-up seconds, confirm each planned stop ends inside 120 s with no group SIGKILL, and check that no `claude -p` outlives the old engine.
- Confirm that any relayed unsent line is not a stale present-tense alarm.

merged.covered:
Lens: process lifecycle and signals at d639d8ec. I found nothing must-fix.

What I read in full:
- supervise.py: main, restart_core, spawn, watch, look, paused, up, stop, core_emit, fall, finish, status, clear_halt, take_lock, _live.
- deadman.Sender.
- news_live.py: run, _run, step, _step, _look_at_stops, check_stops, catch_up_stops, poll_headlines, handle_scored, drain_trial, _beat, _log_trade, score_batch, data._chart/_get_json, journal.append and verify_chain.
- drill_supervisor.py: drills a, b, c, d, f, cloud and cloud-check.
- Spec 4.2-4.5 and the plan's Tasks 19-20.
- Rulings 23, 35-41, 47-53, P2, P5, P18 and 37.

I ran no processes. The engine reasoning comes from the code, plus the tracked news_health.jsonl rows (poll_s_max 1.75 s).

What holds:
- **Child always reaped.** Every return of restart_core happens after the child is reaped. stop() waits after SIGTERM and after SIGKILL. A signal that arrives during a wait, a back-off or a hang stop is checked at the next watch, and the core never spawns after a stop order. The parent's lock is freed only in main's finally, after the child is gone. The exception is an uncaught exception escaping watch(): it frees the lock for a few milliseconds before PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills the engine. I found no such exception on any real input (garbage or torn heartbeat, uptime log, trades, book or state file).
- **Death with the parent.** PR_SET_PDEATHSIG is set from the main thread. An engine whose parent died before the prctl returns 143 on its getppid check, and the top-of-round getppid check backs it up if prctl fails.
- **One parent, one engine.** Both run under an flock on a non-inheritable descriptor. A second parent exits 3, and a refused child exits 3 with lock waits that are not counted.
- **--status order.** It answers kill_stray only when no live parent holds the lock. It never answers launch while /proc/locks shows a live holder, so a woken watchdog cannot start a second parent or engine. A wrongly launched parent exits 3 and writes nothing.
- **Hang kill on a slow engine.** Each stretch without a beat is one bounded call:
  - a Yahoo chart call with 3 retries at timeout 20: up to about 66 s on a blackhole, about 126 s at worst;
  - the scorer, up to 90 s (subprocess.run kills it and does not wait for its pipes);
  - a feed poll: 1.4 s measured, about 100 s on a blackhole;
  - a send, up to 15 s per channel, followed by a beat.

  All of these stay under hang_seconds 180. drill f checks that slow looks raise no hang row.
- **A kill mid-write.** It leaves a torn journal line that the chain tolerates (after_torn), or a stale .tmp file next to an intact book, heartbeat or state file (tmp file plus rename). _log_trade saves the book right after the trade row, so a kill between the two is a tiny window, and start_checks finds it (E1).
- **Machine pause.** Ruling 49 exempts it from the hang rule.
- **Other paths.** --clear-halt is bounded by its timeout and takes the lock briefly. The sender never blocks the loop. finish() is bounded by send_timeout_seconds.
- **Drills.** b and d check the hang kill and the parent kill (d fails on any exit-3 refusal), and cloud-check checks that nothing is left after a stop from outside.

Not checked: which signal TaskStop and the 2-hour cap send. That is only known after the cloud drills. The slot prompts (Task 19) are not in this diff; I judged them against spec 4.4's table.

findings.where: ai-trader/aitrader/supervise.py:1156-1159 (R2 is sent only from up()), 1217-1218 (fall stores ep["r2"]), 1227-1228 (planned end only closes an episode that has an up)
findings.what: With the hang switch on, R2 goes out only at the replacement child's first `up`. If a planned end (handover, signal, orphaned) comes after the hang kill but before that `up`, R2 is never said. No alert row is written for it, so --status `unsent` cannot relay it. The next parent's gap_line measures from the sup_stop row, not from the fall, so the blind time before the kill (at least hang_seconds) is in no line.
findings.scenario: 10:47:50: the engine has written no beat for more than 180 s, gets killed, and a replacement starts at once (ran >= healthy). The market is open and one name is held with no fresh quote. That name enters `blind` only after stop_blind_alert_seconds = 300, so first_look_done stays false and no `up` comes. At 10:48:00 handover_due fires: watch returns "handover", ep["ups"] is empty, Ruling 37's branch sends nothing, and the parent exits 76. The next parent's first up builds R4b, if one is due at all, from the 10:48 sup_stop onward. The owner never reads that the engine hung and was killed. Normally the window is the replacement's 1-3 s boot. It grows to 300 s only when a held name has no quote. With names held, R6 already fired at the replacement's boot beat (Ruling 35), so the owner knows the stops were unchecked. With nothing held, nothing is at risk.
findings.why: The hang kill is the one event that Ruling P5 says R2 reports. Neither P5 nor Ruling 37 covers a planned end before the first up. The rest of the gap goes to R4b, and that line starts counting at the wrong row.
findings.fix: Before the planned-end branch at line 1227, and at the halt, lock_held and crash_loop ends: if ep["r2"] is still set, send R2. Use the kill row's time and a blind_s from the dead engine's last look (kid["last_look"]) to now. If that cannot be built, write an alert row with sent false so the watchdog relays it.
findings.against_ruling: not against a ruling: P5 and 37 do not cover this case; Ruling 37's premise that 'the handover gap measures it' does not hold for a hang kill

verdict.evidence:
The mechanism is real, but the finding's 300 s window is wrong. Reproduced in <SCRATCH>/review-step2/verify-lifecycle/repro/r2_lost.py: dummy run 1 beats then hangs (hang_seconds 2, switch on); run 2 beats but never makes a first look. The parent then ends planned, once by SIGTERM and once by --handover with the clock moved past 10:48. Both logs read: hang (killed_with TERM), exit why=hang, start, code, stale_stops, alert R6, exit why=planned, sup_stop signal/handover. There is no R2 alert row, neither sent nor unsent, so --status cannot relay it. Cause: R2 is said only in up() at supervise.py:1156-1159. The planned-end branch at :1227 needs ep["ups"]. findings.what: After a timely planned stop, the engine's process group is left alone. Trial second-check `claude -p` processes, started by daemon threads under guards "log", outlive the engine. Their 60 s timeout was enforced by the engine's subprocess.run, which died with it. Spec 4.2's 'until its own timeout' is therefore not true once the engine is gone. The hang path already sends SIGKILL to the group (Ruling 36 f).
findings.scenario: 11:59: a headline scored 9 is bought, and _ask_later starts 2 verify calls plus 1 rescore (`claude -p`). At the 12:28 handover the engine stops in a few seconds, drain_trial does not wait, and the engine exits 143. The parent's wait succeeds, so no killpg follows. The `claude -p` processes run on, unparented and unbounded, next to the next engine. They use model quota, CPU and memory until they finish or hit EPIPE on their closed output pipe. They hold no lock and write nothing to state.
findings.why: Soft: these are no engines, but they are unsupervised processes of the old tree. They compete with the new engine on a small machine.
findings.fix: In stop(), after child.wait() returns in the planned branch, call _signal_group(child.pid, SIGKILL), as the hang branch does. Ruling 36(f) already covers why this is safe: the group number stays reserved while it has members.

verdict.evidence:
Reproduced in <SCRATCH>/review-step2/verify-lifecycle/repro/orphan.py: a child starts `sleep 60` in its own process group and exits 143 on SIGTERM. The parent is sent SIGTERM. main returned 143, and the grandchild was still alive in pgid = the child's pid; I then killed it by its pid. The cause is stop()'s planned branch (supervise.py:1184-1191): it calls _signal_group only when child.wait times out.

In the engine, _ask_later starts daemon threads (news_live.py:1416-1436). _ask_second (:1346-1375) runs verify_calls 2 plus 1 rescore, i.e. 3 `claude -p` processes via subprocess.run(timeout=60) (:237, :314). They inherit the engine's group, and the 60 s timeout is enforced only by the engine's thread. drain_trial(wait=0 if market open or STOP) at :2017 does not wait. So after a timely planned stop these processes outlive the engine, and spec 4.2's 'until its own timeout' does not hold.

How far it matters: a trial exists only after a buy, so an orphan needs a buy within about 60 s before a planned stop. Each orphan ends when its model call returns and it writes to the closed stdout pipe (EPIPE), or at claude's own API timeout, so 'unbounded' is overstated. Orphans hold no lock and write no state. The class predates the diff: a bare engine ending in market hours already used wait=0. The landing adds about 4 planned stops a day, and `or STOP.is_set()` extends wait=0 to planned stops after the close. Soft harm, safe one-line fix (Ruling 36 f): minor.

findings.where: ai-trader/scripts/drill_supervisor.py:280-288, :310-312 (bare engines: no --supervised, no tie to the drill's life), :207-211 (signal_child)
findings.what: Cleanup on every exit has one hole. Drill e's bare engine runs with --until 24:00, which never comes, and has nothing that ends it when the drill script is SIGKILLed. Parents end themselves through the orphan check (supervise.py:985-986), but bare engines do not. Separately, signal_child accepts any process whose argv names the stub script, not one of this drill's state directories.
findings.scenario: Task 20 runs `all` at real numbers as a tracked background command for 35-40 min. If the session stops it with TaskStop, or the cap hits, and the signal is SIGKILL to the drill's pid only (which signal is still unknown, and the cloud drill exists to learn it), the engine of drill e's current round keeps polling its stubs in TMPDIR for ever. If the whole group is killed, it dies, because popen sets no new session. For signal_child: the suite's Drills test (a c f --fast) and a background `all` share DUMMY and ENGINE, so a stale heartbeat pid reused by the other run's stub would pass the check (a very small race).
findings.why: The safety rule is 'clean up on every exit, signal only pids it started'. The leak cannot reach the network (tripwire, clean_env), but it never ends.
findings.fix: Start bare engines with `--supervised <os.getpid()>` (PDEATHSIG plus the ppid check; this is also the mode every live engine runs in after tonight). In signal_child, also require that the drill's state path is in the argv (`--state-dir` for the engine, `--heartbeat` for the dummy).

verdict.evidence: Drill.bare (:310-312) starts engine_child with --until 24:00, which the loop's `(now.hour, now.minute) >= (24, 0)` never reaches.
